subject: Post-demo: NexaHealth inference economics & pilot proposal
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: NexaHealth inference economics & pilot proposal

Hi Liam — thanks again for the demo call today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Recap of what we heard from you:
- Primary use: context-aware clinical note summarization for provider inbox (mobile + web).
- Scale target: ~100k MAUs within 12 months; peak concurrency low, but heavy nightly batch summarization for new notes.
- Quality bar: summaries must preserve key meds/alerts; target recall >95% for critical items.

2) Cost/volume signals you shared on call (please correct if I got this wrong):
- Expected active users at launch: 10k–25k in first 3 months
- Avg prompt+response per user/day: ~40 tokens in prompts + ~320 tokens generated -> ~360 tokens/user/day
- Preliminary target spend: $8k–$20k / month for hosted inference initially

3) What we propose as immediate next steps:
- Redwood to send a short unit-econ sketch ($/1M tokens and $/feature) and a pilot SOW with a 3-month evaluation window. (Deliverable: MVP integration + ops dashboard + baseline latency SLO)
- Your team to confirm expected 1M-token target and procurement contacts for a pilot purchase

Attachment: I attached a one-page pricing sketch and a draft SOW for an initial pilot.

If the volume math below matches your expectations, we can aim to lock a pilot PO + access in the next 5 business days.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: NexaHealth_MVP_pricing.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Aisha — quick clarifications and our numbers: 
- The 10k–25k is correct for the early rollout; engineering expects the 100k MAU milestone only by month 12.
- Your token estimate is close; ops measured sample traffic showing 300–380 tokens per active user/day depending on note length.
- Our procurement budget for pilot: we can go up to $18k/mo for a 3-month pilot, ideally closer to $10–12k.

Target economics that stakeholders want to see before sign-off:
- Target cost assumption: $/1M tokens <= $12 to get comfortable with feature unit economics
- Rough expectations on per-feature unit economics: team wants an estimate of $/feature served (avg across mobile/web) and CAC payback under a $12 CPM assumption

Looping in procurement (procurement@nexahealth.com) for contract/PO steps. Will review your attachments and get back with a procurement contact for a PO if numbers look good.

— Liam

Aditya / Marcus — forwarding Liam's clarifications. Procurement wants a PO-level number and their target $/1M tokens <= $12. They can do up to $18k/mo for a 3-month pilot, prefer $10–12k.

Ask: Can you sketch a compact unit-econ note we can send to Liam today? Key bullets we should include: 
- Recommended $/1M token for pilot (hosted) and rationale (latency SLO, caching assumptions)
- Breakout $/feature (assume 360 tokens/user/day, 15% activation rate -> features served per MAU) and CAC payback example for a $100 ACV feature (or different baseline if you prefer)

I attached the draft pricing workbook — please update the pilot sheet and I will share with Liam + procurement.

Short deadline: need a draft by EOD Pacific.

Thanks — Aisha

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NexaHealth numbers — unit econ sketch + pilot pricing recommendation

Aisha / Marcus — quick sketch below (feel free to paste into an email). Assumptions first: 
- Pilot hosted SKU (no private deployment): standard batch+streaming mix, average sequence length 360 tokens, caching reduces 1st-token cost for repeat prefixes by ~12% over time, concurrency low.
- Redwood baseline inference cost (net to customer for hosted, incl. infra/ops margin): $9.50 / 1M tokens for pilot-scale volume (this reflects a modest introductory discount + commitment).

1) Recommended pilot price: $9.50 / 1M tokens (=> at 1M tokens monthly this is $9.50/mo). For NexaHealth's stated budget range, that maps to: 
- At $10k/mo => ~1.05B tokens / month (note: numbers scaled) — hold on, typo: clarify units below. Correct mapping: $9.50/1M => $9,500 per 1B tokens.
- For convenience present as $9.5k per 1B tokens; more useful to show $/1M as requested.

2) $/feature estimate (MVP summarization feature): 
- Assumptions: 360 tokens/user/day => ~10.8M tokens per 30k active users/day (360 * 30k).
- Feature served per active user/day: 1 summary (primary path) => cost per user/day = 360 tokens * ($9.50 / 1,000,000) = $0.00342/day => $0.103 / month (30 days).
- So $/feature (monthly active user served once per day) ~ $0.10. At scale, caching/quantization can push this down ~15–25% depending on model variant.

3) CAC payback example (simple): 
- Assume feature drives $100 ARPA/ARR per new customer (Nexa's product input). If incremental gross margin target is 60% and Redwood inference contributes to cost-of-goods: 
- Per-new-customer monthly inference cost at 1 user (one summary/day) = ~$0.10. Annual inference cost = $1.20. 
- CAC payback driven by total acquisition cost (assume CAC $300 for this channel): payback months = CAC / (monthly gross contribution) = 300 / (ARPA_monthly * margin - inference_cost) => if ARPA_monthly = $8.33 (to hit $100 ARR) and margin = 60% => contribution = $5.00 - $0.10 = $4.90 => CAC payback = 300 / 4.90 = ~61 months (this is long; note this is an example showing inference is tiny relative to CAC).
- Key callout: inference is not the primary driver of CAC payback for this type of feature; the focus is on keeping unit inference cost predictable and bounded to avoid margin erosion at scale.

4) Margin targets & risks: 
- If Nexa needs to hold gross margin >= 55% for the product line, keeping $/1M under $12 gives breathing room vs. model upgrades. Our $9.50 pilot price should meet their $12 target comfortably.
- Risk reserves: add a 10% buffer for unanticipated increased token usage on clinical long-forms and 10% for SLO-backed premium if they require 99th percentile latency <200ms. Recommend contract language for an overage band if actual tokens exceed estimates by >20%.

Recommendation: propose pilot at $9.50 / 1M tokens, 3-month term, $10k/month minimum guarantee (covers baseline operations and gives them seats to test). That lands inside their procurement sweet spot and preserves margin headroom.

I can drop numbers into the attached workbook; Marcus can prepare a 1-pager for procurement/legal.

- Aditya

- Pilot length: 3 months
- Price: $9.50 per 1M tokens (hosted)
- Minimum monthly commitment: $10,000 / month (covers baseline infra and support)
- Inclusions: integration assistance, observability dashboard, 2 SLOs (p95 latency and availability), weekly check-ins and a performance report at end of pilot
- Overage: usage above committed tokens billed at the same price; if monthly usage exceeds estimate by >20% we reserve the right to propose a scaling addendum
